items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: We put this big band together... Another guy by the name of Prince (PHONETIC), that worked for -- he was a tenor saxophone player.

ctx.x: Johnny Miller (PHONETIC) was his bass. No, no, no, no. He had -- Wesley Prince was his bassist. Oscar Moore was the guitar player. We put this big band together and we had a battle of bands down Broadway on Labor Day, 1939, with the Lunceford Band, the Basie Band and the L.A. big band, which I was the leader of. When we finished coming back, Lionel Hampton was in town with Benny Goodman, so we pulled the truck past Lionel Hampton's house and we played a number for him. He was so enthralled about the whole thing,…

own band, he called me and tried to get the same band that he had on that truck that day that we went by, which was incorporated as King Cole was my piano player and his complete trio was part of the thing.
